answer: Require every agent to post a refundable bond that is slashed if it signs conflicting claims, and let peers accept a claim only after independent bonded agents attest to it. One identity is cheap to mint, but each apparent participant must lock real capital; splitting one actor into a plume of aliases therefore multiplies the bond needed to sway a quorum. The bridge from reputation to influence is costly: an attacker risks forfeiting funds, while the ocean of possible fake names gives no advantage unless those names can also finance distinct bonds.
